blocks.title: After this PDF you can
bullets: choose the correct subjunctive tense after any main verb (sequence of tenses)
use the imperfect subjunctive in noun, adverbial and relative clauses
express wishes with ojalá (possible, unlikely and impossible)
recognise the -se forms of the imperfect subjunctive in written Spanish

blocks.text: The subjunctive tense depends on the tense of the main verb and on when the subordinate action happens.

head: Main verb
Subjunctive tense
Example
rows: Me ha pedido que le ayude.

blocks.title: Rule of thumb
blocks.text: Present world, present subjunctive. Past world (preterite, imperfect, past perfect, conditional), imperfect subjunctive. Before the subordinate verb, ask yourself which world the main verb lives in.

head: Present
Past
English
rows: I want / wanted you to come.
I doubt / doubted it is / was true.
Me alegro de que estés aquí.
Me alegré de que estuvieras aquí.
I am / was glad you are / were here.
It is / was important that you know.
I do not / did not think he would arrive.
Ask / I asked him to help.

items: Wishes and orders: Mi madre quería que estudiara medicina. Nos pidió que esperáramos.
Emotions: Me molestó que no me llamaras. Sentí que se fuera.
Doubt and denial: No pensaba que fuera tan caro. Dudaban que ganáramos.
Impersonal expressions: Era necesario que todos firmaran. Fue una pena que no vinieras.
Conditional main verb: Sería mejor que te quedaras. Preferiría que no dijeras nada.

blocks.title: Present subjunctive after a past verb?
blocks.text: Sometimes a present subjunctive follows a past main verb when the result is still true now: Me pidió que le ayude esta tarde. (He asked me, and the help is still to come.) In most cases, and in exams, use the imperfect: Me pidió que le ayudara.

head: Clause type
Example
English
rows: Lo explicó despacio para que lo entendiéramos.
He explained slowly so that we would understand.
Dijo que llamaría en cuanto llegara.
He said he would call as soon as he arrived.
Even if it rained, we would go.
No había nadie que lo supiera.
There was nobody who knew it.
Buscaba un piso que tuviera balcón.
I was looking for a flat with a balcony (any).
Hablaba como si lo supiera todo.
He talked as if he knew everything.
I would like to ask for the bill.

blocks.title: Specific vs unspecific
blocks.text: Tenía un piso que tenía balcón (I had one, specific: indicative). Buscaba un piso que tuviera balcón (not yet found: subjunctive). The same contrast exists in the present: Busco un piso que tenga balcón.
Ojalá (I hope, if only) always takes the subjunctive. The tense shows how likely the wish is.

head: Tense
Example
Meaning
rows: If only I had more time (unlikely).
If only he had come (too late).

items: Ojalá que is also correct: Ojalá que no llueva.
Pluperfect subjunctive is formed with hubiera + participle (more in PDF 2).

blocks.text: The imperfect subjunctive has a second set of endings: -se, -ses, -se, -semos, -seis, -sen. It is used in writing and formal speech; in Spain both forms are fully correct. The two forms are interchangeable, except that the polite quisiera / pudiera use only -ra.

blocks.title: Which one in Spain?
blocks.text: Both forms are correct in Spain. -ra is the usual choice in speech, and -se appears more in literary and formal writing: Si tuviera / tuviese tiempo, iría. In your own writing, one form is enough: pick -ra and stay consistent.

rows: Doubt in the past: imperfect subjunctive.
No había nadie que lo sabía.
No había nadie que lo supiera.
Buscaba un piso que tenía balcón.
Buscaba un piso que tuviera balcón.
Habló como si es el jefe.
Habló como si fuera el jefe.
antes de que: subjunctive, past: imperfect.

blocks.text: Fill in the correct subjunctive form. Answers are on the last page.

items.q: Mi madre quería que yo ______ medicina.
items.full: Mi madre quería que yo estudiara medicina.

items.q: Nos pidió que ______ en la puerta.
items.full: Nos pidió que esperáramos en la puerta.

items.q: Me alegré de que ______ en la fiesta.
items.full: Me alegré de que estuvieras en la fiesta.

items.q: No había nadie que ______ la respuesta.
items.full: No había nadie que supiera la respuesta.
Buscaba un piso que tuviera balcón.
Hablaba como si lo supiera todo.

items.q: Sería mejor que te ______ en casa.
items.full: Sería mejor que te quedaras en casa.
Salió antes de que nosotros llegáramos.

items.q: Me ha pedido que le ______ esta tarde.
items.full: Me ha pedido que le ayude esta tarde.

items.q: If only I had more money.

items.a: No había nadie que lo supiera.
